questions.question_text:
An investor holds $1400$ shares in a mining firm.
The firm declares a dividend of $\$0.32$ per share.
What is the total dividend payment?

options.why: Treated 32 cents as 0.032 dollars.
Divided the share count by the dividend per share.
Added the dividend to the share count.

questions.question_text:
A shareholder received $\$630$ in annual dividends from $1800$ shares.
What was the dividend paid per share?

options.why: Divided shares by total dividend instead of dividend by shares.
Arithmetic error in division.
Misplaced decimal place by multiplying by 10.

questions.question_text:
A share has a market price of $\$20.00$ and pays an annual dividend of $\$0.84$ per share.
What is the dividend yield?

options.why: This is approximately $20\div0.84$, the reversed ratio without the percentage conversion. Yield is $0.84\div20\times100\%=4.2\%$.
The correct calculation is $0.84\div20\times100\%=4.2\%$; $8.4\%$ is twice that result.
Forgot to multiply by 100 to convert to a percentage.

questions.question_text:
A share is currently trading at $\$15.00$ and pays a dividend of $75\text{ cents}$ per share.
What is the dividend yield?

options.why: Substituted 75 cents as 7.50 dollars.
Omitted multiplication by 100 percent.
This uses the reversed ratio $15\div0.75=20$ and labels it as a percentage. Yield uses $0.75\div15\times100\%=5\%$.

questions.question_text:

What is the total dividend payment?

options.why: Calculated 6% of share price on 1000 shares instead of 1600.
Divided total value by 100 instead of calculating dividend.
Gave dividend per share rather than total dividend.

questions.question_text:
A stock pays an annual dividend of $\$0.40$ per share.
How many shares are needed to earn $\$920$ in annual dividend income?

options.why: Multiplied 920 by 0.40 instead of dividing.
Misplaced decimal place by dividing by 4 instead of 0.40.
Multiplied by 4 instead of dividing by 0.40.

questions.question_text:
An investor purchases $2500$ shares for a total cost of $\$37\,500$.
The company pays a total annual dividend of $\$1875$ on these shares.
What is the dividend yield?

options.why: Forgot to multiply by 100 to convert to a percentage.
Dividing total dividend by the number of shares gives $1875\div2500=\$0.75$ per share, not $7.5\%$. Divide this by $\$15$ and multiply by $100\%$ to find yield.
This is the reversed total-value ratio $37\,500\div1875=20$, labelled as a percentage. The dividend-to-share-value ratio gives $1875\div37\,500\times100\%=5\%$.

questions.question_text:
An investor owns $800$ shares in Company X (market price $\$6.00$, dividend yield $5\%$) and $n$ shares in Company Y (market price $\$12.00$, dividend yield $4.5\%$).
If the total annual dividend is $\$510$, find $n$.

options.why: Company Y must supply $510-240=\$270$. At $\$0.54$ per share this needs $500$ shares; $400$ shares supply only $\$216$.
Arithmetic error in subtracting Company X dividend.
$450$ shares would supply $450\times0.54=\$243$, below the required $\$270$. The required number is $270\div0.54=500$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Dividend X} = 800 \times (0.05 \times 6.00) = 800 \times 0.30 = \$240$
$\text{Dividend Y} = 510 - 240 = \$270$
$\text{Dividend Y per share} = 0.045 \times 12.00 = \$0.54$
$n = \frac{270}{0.54} = 500\text{ shares}$
